title: Korean convenience chains launch June sports-and-summer discount blitz - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: The three major convenience store chains are rolling out large-scale promotions in June targeting demand for sports viewing and early summer outings. They are highlighting popular summer items, from discounts on chicken, pizza, and beer timed to the Korea soccer schedule to promotions on ice cream, highballs, and fresh-brewed instant coffee. GS25 will run chicken, pizza, beer, and snack promotions centered on Korea's soccer match days on the 12th, 19th, and 25th throughout June. For chicken, from 8 p.m. the day before each game through game day, three made-to-order items—boneless fried chicken, whole mozzarella cheese chicken, and whole fried chicken—will be sold at a 50% discount. Buffalo wing sticks will be offered as a buy one, get one free deal. Go Pizza will give a 40% discount when buying two or more pies on the 12th and 19th, and a 50% discount on the 25th. Beer promotions will also run in parallel. Throughout June, GS25 will sell six cans of seven popular beers, including Daisy Lager, for 12,000 won to customers paying with KB Kookmin or Shinhan cards. When purchasing beer bundle products with Kakao Pay, a 20% payback benefit will be provided, and on the day before and the day of games, beer bundle pickup deals—four cans for 8,000 won and six cans for 12,000 won—will also be offered through the "Our Neighborhood GS" app. About 30 snack items, including jerky and dried filefish, will be 50% off when buying two through the 15th. Distributors under GS Retail are also helping build a supportive soccer atmosphere. GS The Fresh will hang banners reading "Cheer for Korea" in stores and run app pre-order time deals on the morning of game days through the "Our Neighborhood GS" app. GS Shop will hold the "GOAL-den Festa" from the 12th to the 25th and give chicken e-gift cards to 100 customers each day who spend more than 50,000 won across all channels. CU, run by BGF Retail, is focusing on discounts for key summer products such as beer, highballs, ice cream, and fresh-brewed instant coffee as the summer season gets into full swing. Domestic canned beers Hanmac and Kelly will be sold eight for 16,000 won, lowering the per-can price to around 2,000 won. The top-selling imported beer bundle, Asahi 6-pack, will be offered at 12,900 won, and bundles of four cans of popular imports such as Stella, Heineken, and Hoegaarden will be sold for 10,000 won. Highball promotions will also expand. The CU-exclusive Jim Beam Highball Peach will be sold at more than 40% off at four cans for 9,000 won. Differentiated items such as Absolut fresh fruit highball, aespa lemonade highball, and Peaceminusone highball can be purchased at 12,000 won when buying three cans. An additional 2,000 won discount applies when paying with Naver Pay Money or points. Ice cream promotions were also strengthened. All Häagen-Dazs products will have up to 50% off when buying two or more. Eleven popular bar ice creams from Binggrae, including B.B.BIG, Nougat Bar, and Babamba, will be sold for 5,600 won when buying 10. When purchasing get Coffee iced Americano together with a sandwich, hamburger, or salad, customers can get up to 1,500 won off depending on the payment card. 7-Eleven also put ready-to-eat chicken and ready-to-eat pizza promotions at the forefront for the international soccer event and the peak summer season. Throughout June, 7-Eleven will run a 2+1 deal on jumbo drumsticks and red bean glutinous rice donuts, and will give a free cola when purchasing a consomme boneless chicken set. During key match periods, buffalo wing drums will be discounted by 2,000 won. When buying 11 ready-to-eat chicken items for same-day pickup through the Seven App, customers can receive discounts of up to 4,000 won per item. Also throughout June, when paying with Kakao Pay Money, "whole thigh chicken steak" and "giant chicken cutlet" will be offered at 20% off, and starting on the 12th, "fried whole chicken 720g" will be sold at 30% off. Ready-to-eat pizza promotions were also prepared. When purchasing any of five whole ready-to-eat pizza products, including ALL pepperoni pizza and bulgogi truffle pizza, a cola will be provided, and pepperoni slice pizza and combination slice pizza will be offered as a cross buy one, get one free deal. title: "Energy Powers Everyday Life"... GS Caltex Hosts Online Family Art Exhibition - 아시아경제
content:
"Energy Powers Everyday Life"... GS Caltex Hosts Online Family Art Exhibition On June 1, GS Caltex announced the launch of the online exhibition “Energy Gallery,” which showcases artworks submitted to its employee family-participation cultural program, the “GS Caltex Art Festa.” GS Caltex ‘Energy Gallery’ Exhibition Hall Screen Capture. GS Caltex Website This exhibition was organized in celebration of Family Month in May. It features works created by employees’ children in collaboration with their parents, reflecting on the meaning of energy. The exhibition adds vibrancy to the artworks using artificial intelligence (AI) technology. The exhibited pieces were created under the theme “Stories of Energy That Move Our Everyday Lives.” Participating children selected one of three topics to express through their art: peaceful daily life powered by energy; energy guardians who light up the world; and new energy worlds of the future. The artworks capture family conversations about energy and the imaginative ideas of children. The pieces depict a wide range of scenes, from family gatherings under a bright lamp at dinner, to energy heroes illuminating the city, to future cities powered by eco-friendly technology. GS Caltex used AI technology to animate the artworks. GS Caltex expects that this exhibition will provide an opportunity for parents and children to reflect on and share the meaning of energy and work together. A GS Caltex representative said, “The energy we create brightens someone’s day, powers the routines of families, and sustains communities across society. We hope that the Energy Gallery serves as an opportunity to convey the value of energy through the eyes of children.” GS Caltex continues to support culture and the arts through initiatives such as operating the GS Caltex Yeulmaru cultural arts space and sponsoring the GS Art Center. The exhibition is open to all and can be viewed in the Energy Gallery section of GS Caltex’s official Media Hub. © The Asia Business Daily(www.asiae.co.kr). All rights reserved. title: GS Global Conducts Cemetery Cleanup and Supports Childcare Facility - 아시아경제
content:
GS Global Conducts Cemetery Cleanup and Supports Childcare Facility GS Global announced on June 1 that, ahead of Patriots and Veterans Month in June, the company visited the Seoul National Cemetery in Dongjak-gu, Seoul, on May 27 to honor the sacrifice of fallen patriots and national heroes by conducting volunteer activities to clean and beautify the cemetery grounds. Approximately 40 executives and employees from the Corporate Strategy Office, including Sungwon Kim, CEO of GS Global, are taking a commemorative photo after volunteering at 'Jacob's House.' GS On that day, approximately 40 executives and employees from the Financial Management Office, including Kim Sungwon, CEO of GS Global, participated in the volunteer work. After paying their respects at the Memorial Tower, the employees visited the gravesites, where they cleaned headstones, removed weeds, and tidied up the surrounding areas, reflecting on the meaning of patriotism and remembrance. Continuing their efforts during Family Month in May, on May 29 they visited "Jacob's House," a childcare facility located in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, to carry out additional volunteer activities. CEO Kim and about 40 executives and employees from the Corporate Strategy Office joined the children for lunch, fostering emotional exchange, and engaged in practical indoor and outdoor improvement activities. These included plogging (an eco-friendly activity where one walks or jogs while picking up litter) around the facility and installing window blinds to improve the living environment for the children. GS Global's social contribution efforts are meaningful in that they go beyond simple financial support and actively involve employee participation. A GS Global representative stated, "In order to fulfill our corporate social responsibility, we connected cemetery cleaning activities for patriots and support for childcare by having our employees participate directly," adding, "We will continue to pursue social contribution activities that provide tangible benefits to the nation and local communities, and spread positive influence." © The Asia Business Daily(www.asiae.co.kr). title: Baekseok Signature Xi Bridges Buldang New Town and Seongseong District Infrastructure - 조선일보
content: 1,174-Household Complex Features Skylounge, Proximity to Schools, Industrial Sites, and Parks GS Engineering & Construction is launching the sale of the ‘Baekseok Signature Xi’ in Baekseok 5 District, Baekseok-dong, Seobuk-gu, Cheonan, Chungcheongnam-do, this month. The Baekseok Signature Xi, developed through the Baekseok 5 District urban development project, will be built as a large complex spanning from the basement 2nd floor to the 28th floor above ground, comprising 13 buildings and a total of 1,174 households (Block 1: 854 households, Block 2: 320 households). All households are allocated for general sale and are divided by exclusive area as follows: 59㎡ (50 households), 63㎡ (27 households), 74㎡ (196 households), 84㎡ (819 households), 99㎡ (78 households), and 115㎡ (4 households). Baekseok-dong, located between Buldang New Town and Seongseong District, has recently gained attention as a residential area that can simultaneously utilize the infrastructure of both regions. A source from the sales department stated, “The Baekseok Signature Xi is a large-scale brand apartment complex supplied to the Baekseok-dong area after a long time, so demand from buyers is very high.” ◇Enjoying Infrastructure and Natural Environment Simultaneously The Baekseok Signature Xi is situated in a living zone connecting Buldang-dong, Seongjeong-dong, and Dujung-dong, allowing residents to utilize existing urban infrastructure. Large distribution facilities such as Costco, E-Mart, E-Mart Traders, and Lotte Mart are located near the complex, providing excellent living conditions. Administrative and cultural facilities, including Cheonan City Hall, Galleria Department Store, and Cheonan Sports Complex, are within driving distance. The proximity to Songgol Park, Notaesan Mountain, and Notae Neighborhood Park offers the advantage of enjoying both urban infrastructure and a pleasant natural environment. Well-developed nearby roads make vehicle travel convenient. Major roads such as Yeongbong-ro and Baekseok-ro are nearby, and access to the Gyeongbu Expressway’s Cheonan IC is easy. The KTX Cheonan-Asan Station is also close, facilitating travel to other regions. The educational environment is excellent, with schools and academies well-established in the vicinity. Hanseol Elementary School, Hwanseo Elementary School, and Hwanseo Middle School are within walking distance, ensuring safe commutes. The Baekseok-dong academy district is accessible on foot, and the Buldang-dong academy district, recognized as the largest in Chungcheongnam-do, is also nearby. The proximity to major corporations in Cheonan, such as Samsung SDI, Samsung Electronics, and Samsung Display, is another strength, enabling work-residence proximity. The Cheonan 2nd, 3rd, and 4th General Industrial Complexes, the Foreigner-Exclusive Industrial Complex, and the Baekseok Agricultural Industrial Complex are also nearby. The interior design applies structures preferred by residents. All households feature a 4-bay cross-ventilation layout (living room and three bedrooms aligned in the same direction) to ensure ample lighting and ventilation. Depending on the unit type, additional spaces such as alpha rooms, pantries (small storage areas), and dressing rooms have been included to expand storage capacity. The complex will also feature ‘Club Xi-an,’ a specialized community facility unique to Xi apartments, offering abundant amenities for residents. Facilities include a fitness center, sauna, cafe lounge, sunken plaza, study room, small library, indoor golf practice range, screen golf, and guesthouse. A skylounge will be built on the 28th floor of Building 101. A GS Engineering & Construction official stated, “The Baekseok Signature Xi has excellent location advantages, allowing residents to enjoy both the Buldang New Town and the old downtown living zones. As a Xi apartment complex entering Baekseok-dong, where large-scale apartment supplies have been rare, we are putting great effort into preparing the product.” The model house for the Baekseok Signature Xi will be located in 1517, Buldang-dong, Seobuk-gu, Cheonan, Chungcheongnam-do. Move-in is scheduled for 2029.

title: The Suzuki ADV That Feels As Reliable As A Honda And As Comfortable As A GS - Top Speed
content:
The adventure motorcycle segment has a pecking order, and the European badges sit at the top of it. Reputation for a brand compounds over decades of delivering great products. And then, when a group of enthusiasts meets up on a Sunday morning ride, that reputation is discussed, spread, and reinforced by more prospective buyers. This dynamic, however, keeps capable bikes overlooked and the inflated prices of alternatives a bit defensible, barring a few exceptions. What also makes it the basis of comfort considerations is exactly where the two ideas converge. Lower combustion temperatures mean that less heat reaches the rider. That’s one engineering decision, and two consequences that matter to the same rider on the same long day. The comfort hardware builds upon this theme. Long-travel, fully adjustable suspension at both ends does not usually get specified for a machine whose development stopped at the first viable product. Independent compression and rebound tuning at each wheel exists because a fixed damping stops tracking the road when pace, load, or surface quality changes. All of these are accumulated answers to the questions that riders have sent back across two decades of ownership that have made the V-Strom so well-balanced as an ADV. That makes it the ideal pick here, offering Honda reliability and GS comfort. These overlooked adventure bikes offer a lot of value to those looking for a reliable motorcycle And Suzuki has listened, while silently integrating these changes to build the latest iteration of the V-Strom. This is one of the reasons why the most overlooked adventure bike that will last a lifetime is typically the one without a European badge, and the V-Strom has spent a good part of two decades making that true. The platform launched back in 2002, and the DE variant arrived a whole two decades later in 2023. It brought with it a 21-inch front wheel, more ground clearance, extended suspension travel, and the touring fundamentals that were built solid with the standard 1050. At $16,449 for 2026, this competent ADV package is priced below every European rival at this capability level. The 1037cc DOHC V-twin with its 90-degree cylinder angle achieves primary balance without a counterbalancer shaft, something that has carried on from the SV650’s V-twin. That’s one fewer rotating assembly part accumulating wear over a high-mileage ownership cycle. Then there is the heat management referred to earlier that also benefits the rider. And finally, the Suzuki Composite Electrochemical Material (SCEM) cylinder bore coating that reduces friction to further improve the engine’s performance and smoothness. Suzuki bolts the unit directly to the twin-spar frame because the inherent balance makes rubber mounting unnecessary, and the chassis is stiffer for it. Peak output is 107 horsepower and 73.76 lb-ft of torque, with the latter sitting in the mid-range, the ideal place for highway pace for cruising as well as effortless overtakes without downshifts. A 5.3-gallon tank puts the range beyond the distance most riders want to sit for before stopping anyway. Browsing every Suzuki V-Strom model ranked by power across the lineup, the 1050DE sits at the apex, and that position reflects the accumulated refinement as much as displacement. The most powerful adventure bike on this list is an exotic Italian with 170 horsepower. A reliable engine is only as good as an equally robust chassis that carries it. And this is a chassis that’s specifically calibrated for adventures that often demand luggage carrying capacity and/or a pillion. The KYB inverted front fork may not be among the most advanced suspension systems in the world, but it offers just what’s needed. Independent compression, preload, and rebound adjustment not only keeps the front-end customizable to be dialed-in for a rider but also accounts for the added load, if and when needed. A pillion and luggage shift the shock inputs beyond what preload alone can address, so proper fine-tuning of the suspension behavior is an added plus. A KYB link-type rear shock handles full preload and rebound adjustment as well, and Load Dependent Control within the Suzuki Intelligent Ride System (S.I.R.S) manages braking balance automatically when extra weight comes aboard. Suzuki positions the 554-pound heft centrally through the twin-spar frame, and the 1050DE responds to steering inputs more readily than one would expect. The 21-inch front wheel and the DE's extended swingarm hold predictable behavior across surface changes over days and miles on the road. These adventure motorcycles pack in so much tech, NASA would go green with envy S.I.R.S. is where the accumulated engineering decisions are managed from a single system. Traction control runs a dedicated Gravel mode calibrated to a different intervention threshold than what dry asphalt warrants, permitting controlled rear wheel slip on loose surfaces rather than cutting power at the wrong moment. Switchable rear ABS disengages independently of the front on unpaved sections, keeping technical surfaces manageable without removing the front braking safety net. Then there is Hill Hold Control that maintains brake pressure on a grade long enough to remove the balance act from a loaded uphill restart. Back on pavement, the same system shifts without the rider changing anything. Motion Track ABS runs through the six-axis Bosch IMU to extend the ABS function through lean angles. Cruise control holds highway pace without sustained wrist tension. The bidirectional quickshifter handles gear changes in both directions without the clutch, operating as consistently through urban traffic as at open-road speeds. And finally, a 5-inch TFT display puts all of it within a glance, and a USB port at the instrument cluster alongside a 12V outlet under the seat keeps the mobile devices charged. These adventure bikes offer unrivaled everyday practicality. That's not something many ADVs can claim! At that price, the DE sits $2,174 above the 2026 BMW F 900 GS's base of $14,275. While the BMW is definitely an upgrade over the smaller V-Strom, the F 900 GS's 895cc parallel twin makes 105 hp and 68.6 lb-ft of torque at 6,750 rpm, pulling 5 lb-ft less than the V-Strom 1050DE at a higher engine speed. The GS fuel tank also holds a lower 3.8 gallons, 1.5 gallons shorter per fill on a loaded touring day. Both are tiny aspects to consider as they build up over distances. The 2026 Honda Africa Twin CRF1100L at $15,999 makes a closer contest. On paper, this Suzuki delivers Africa Twin-level performance and then some despite the Africa Twin making 101 hp and 83 lb-ft of torque at 5,500 rpm. At approximately 500 pounds, it also runs about 50 pounds lighter. These are real advantages for a rider whose priority is off-road agility over highway miles, but then there’s the case of the parallel-twin, which cannot replicate a 90-degree V-twin’s natural primary balance. At $450 over the Africa Twin and $1,179 over the GS all-in, the V-Strom 1050DE has the character, the slightly better tank range, and decades of platform development to come out on top, albeit being easily overlooked and underappreciated. title: Karol G’s Bikini Top Peeks Through See-Through Natalia Fedner Chain Top - AOL.com
content: Karol G always knows just how to make her mark with unique fashion statements. title: Becky G’s D&G Lingerie Adds Ridiculously Sultry Touch to Her ‘EPA’ MV - AOL.com
content: Becky Gturned up the heat in her “EPA” music video with a daring vintage-inspired lingerie look that blended Y2K styling with bold Latin-pop energy. The singer wore a red and white Dolce & Gabbana paisley lingerie set layered beneath a dramatically unbuttoned mini skirt, creating one of the standout fashion moments from her video. The matching bra and underwear set featured a bandana-inspired paisley print in crimson and white panels. It was trimmed with delicate lace edging for a softer, feminine finish. The balconette-style bra added structure while keeping the styling playful and provocative, especially when paired with the low-waisted skirt that intentionally exposed the coordinating bottoms underneath. Becky layered the lingerie with a cropped white beaded bolero from Sass & Bide’s Resort 2011 collection. The dramatic fringe detailing moved with every dance step, adding texture and motion throughout the market scenes in the video. The combination of fringe and visible lingerie gave the outfit a nostalgic early-2000s aesthetic. In several scenes, Becky styled the lingerie set with a cargo-inspired mini skirt left almost entirely unbuttoned at the waist. This allowed the paisley underwear to become part of the actual outfit rather than being hidden underneath. The styling choice leaned into the ongoing exposed-lingerie trend currently dominating celebrity fashion. She accessorized the look with brown rectangular Chanel rhinestone-logo sunglasses and a gold minimal waist chain belt, both of which elevated the outfit’s vintage glam feel. Becky G completed her look with brown suede fringe boots. The fringe is tied back to the bolero, making the look feel cohesive. Her makeup and hair actually completed the aesthetic. She opted for voluminous dark waves, bronzed makeup, glossy nude lips, and sharply defined eyes. Combined with the bustling market backdrop and energetic choreography, the outfit captured the bold, confident spirit of the music video.
